metadata.title: Casualty Apportionment Database -- All Corps, Both Sides
metadata.purpose: Provides per-tick casualty scaling for the animation engine. Unit visual length = base_length * (1 - cumulative_casualty_rate_to_this_tick). Casualties distributed across ticks within each engagement period using a bell-curve intensity model weighted toward peak action ticks.

formulas.current_strength: initial_strength - sum(casualties assigned to ticks 1 through current_tick)
formulas.destroyed_unit_display: Single dot at last known position if strength drops below 10

sources: Busey, John W. and Martin, David G. -- Regimental Strengths and Losses at Gettysburg (Longstreet House, 1994)
OR Vol. 27, Parts I and II

engagement_periods.notes: Nearly all I Corps casualties fell in a 3-hour window July 1 -- one of the most compressed casualty periods of the battle.
Vermont Brigade casualties during double enfilade on Pickett's right and Wilcox.

engagements: Pickett's Charge repulse at Cemetery Ridge and The Angle
engagement_periods.notes: Cushing's battery (25 casualties), Woodruff's battery (11), Brown's battery (16), and Webb's brigade all suffered heavily at The Angle.
Nearly ALL III Corps casualties fell in approximately 2 hours -- one of the most compressed casualty periods of the battle. Sickles's unauthorized advance created this vulnerability.
VI Corps served as army reserve and saw almost no direct action despite being the largest Union corps present.
XI Corps routed July 1. Many casualties were captures rather than killed/wounded during the retreat through Gettysburg.

engagements: Culp's Hill July 2 evening -- Johnson's assault on Greene's lone brigade
Culp's Hill July 3 morning -- 7-hour fight to recapture Confederate-occupied works
engagement_periods.notes: Colgrove's charge (2nd MA and 27th IN) accounts for a significant share of Day 3 XII Corps casualties.

engagements: Buford's dismounted defense on McPherson's and Herr ridges
Pickett's Charge -- Garnett, Kemper, Armistead brigades
engagement_periods.notes: Pickett's division alone suffered ~2,700 casualties -- 49% of its strength -- in approximately 30 minutes of close combat.

engagements: Culp's Hill morning fight -- 7 hours of combat to hold captured Union works
engagement_periods.notes: Steuart's brigade suffered 42.5% casualties across all three days -- highest in Johnson's division.

engagements: McPherson's Ridge (Heth -- Archer captured, Davis Railroad Cut)
Seminary Ridge (Perrin breakthrough, Scales devastated, Lane drives I Corps)
Wilcox and Lang advance on Cemetery Ridge
Pettigrew-Trimble charge (left column of Pickett-Pettigrew-Trimble assault)
engagement_periods.notes: 26th NC (Pettigrew's brigade) suffered 588 casualties across Days 1 and 3 combined -- highest Confederate regimental total.

engagements: East Cavalry Field -- Hampton wounded, Stuart repulsed by Gregg and Custer

most_compressed_union.note: Nearly 4,200 casualties in approximately 2 hours on July 2 afternoon -- the most compressed major corps casualty period of the battle.

most_compressed_confederate.note: Approximately 2,700 casualties in 30 minutes during Pickett's Charge -- the most intense 30-minute casualty period of the battle.

longest_sustained_action.note: Seven hours of continuous fighting July 3 morning -- the longest sustained infantry combat of the battle.

union.note: 1st Minnesota -- 224 of 262 casualties in 15 minutes July 2

confederate.note: 26th North Carolina -- 588 of 843 casualties across July 1 and 3
